Concept Description: One sitting blood pressure reading or summary at one visit: the systolic and diastolic values taken together. Use when a source records systolic and diastolic as a pair (first, second, third reading, or the average of repeats); not for ankle-brachial index or carotid distensibility, which are separate concepts. The set carries only participant, visit and the member observations; position, site, method and any average/maximum qualifier are set on each member, and the two members must share them.

Concept Description: Spirometry results from one test session at one visit, delivered in the shared spirometry file: FEV1, FVC and the FEV1/FVC ratio, plus the reference-equation predicted values and percent-predicted values when the source provides them. Use for sources that give one set of spirometry per visit with no pre/post split, or that keep pre- and post-bronchodilator results inside the same file (only COPDGene has both, with Context BEFORE and AFTER; HCHS/SOL has pre-bronchodilator values with Context BEFORE; ARIC and the other cohorts carry no bronchodilator Context); not for cohorts delivered in the separate pre-bronchodilator and post-bronchodilator files (SPIROMICS, LTRC). The plain FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC members take pre-bronchodilator values AND values whose bronchodilator status the source does not state; an unstated status is recorded as unknown (no Context). Bronchodilator status is carried on each member (see Metadata), not on the set. Other spirometry concepts (FEV0.5, FEV0.75, FEV3, FEV6, their ratios and height indices) are stand-alone observations that may sit in the same set when the source reports them for the same session. Output file follows the cohort's existing gold layout: cohorts that gold delivers as separate pre- and post-bronchodilator files (SPIROMICS, LTRC) write to spirometry_pre_bd and spirometry_post_bd; every other cohort writes all spirometry members, pre- and post-bronchodilator alike, to spirometry (COPDGene keeps both pre and post there; HCHS/SOL writes its pre-bronchodilator values there). JUDGMENT CALL: a new cohort with no gold uses the separate files only if its source delivers pre- and post-bronchodilator results as separate tables; otherwise spirometry.

Concept Description: Spirometry measured before any bronchodilator was given, at one visit: FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC. Use when the source names the pre-bronchodilator result and a post-bronchodilator result exists for the same visit; not for post-bronchodilator values. Gold writes this set to its own file for SPIROMICS and LTRC, with Context activity_type BRONCHODILATOR_MEDICATION_USE and relative_timing BEFORE on every member. Members use the plain FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC concepts (there are no separate pre-bronchodilator concepts); inside this set, for SPIROMICS and LTRC, they are written to spirometry_pre_bd, not to the member concepts' own file (spirometry). Other cohorts with pre-bronchodilator values (COPDGene, HCHS/SOL) keep them in spirometry with Context BEFORE. Output file follows the cohort's existing gold layout: cohorts that gold delivers as separate pre- and post-bronchodilator files (SPIROMICS, LTRC) write to spirometry_pre_bd and spirometry_post_bd; every other cohort writes all spirometry members, pre- and post-bronchodilator alike, to spirometry (COPDGene keeps both pre and post there; HCHS/SOL writes its pre-bronchodilator values there). JUDGMENT CALL: a new cohort with no gold uses the separate files only if its source delivers pre- and post-bronchodilator results as separate tables; otherwise spirometry.
Example source variable description: Pre-bronchodilator Forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1)|Pre-bronchodilator Forced vital capacity (FVC)

Concept Description: Spirometry measured after a bronchodilator was given, at one visit: FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC. Use for the post-bronchodilator values that define fixed airflow obstruction (post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.70 under GOLD); not for pre-bronchodilator values. Gold writes this set to its own file for SPIROMICS and LTRC, with Context activity_type BRONCHODILATOR_MEDICATION_USE and relative_timing AFTER on every member. JUDGMENT CALL: members are named with the separate post bronchodilator concepts, but gold emits the plain FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC observation_type codes with Context AFTER (see questions). The post-bronchodilator concepts' own output file spirometry_post_bd applies to cohorts delivered with separate pre/post files (SPIROMICS, LTRC); COPDGene keeps its post-bronchodilator members in spirometry (Context AFTER), and moving them is only a proposal (see questions). Percent-predicted values computed from a post-bronchodilator measurement are not members: they stay FEV1, FVC or FEV1/FVC Percent Predicted with Context AFTER. Output file follows the cohort's existing gold layout: cohorts that gold delivers as separate pre- and post-bronchodilator files (SPIROMICS, LTRC) write to spirometry_pre_bd and spirometry_post_bd; every other cohort writes all spirometry members, pre- and post-bronchodilator alike, to spirometry (COPDGene keeps both pre and post there; HCHS/SOL writes its pre-bronchodilator values there). JUDGMENT CALL: a new cohort with no gold uses the separate files only if its source delivers pre- and post-bronchodilator results as separate tables; otherwise spirometry.

Concept Description: The reference-equation (expected) spirometry values for one participant at one visit: predicted FEV0.5, FEV1, FEV1/FVC, FEV3, FEV6 and FVC. Use for values the cohort computed from a reference equation (for example Hankinson/NHANES III) from age, sex, height and race/ethnicity; not for measured values or for percent of predicted. JUDGMENT CALL: V2 lists these six as MeasurementObservationSet rows, but each has one OMOP code, one value and one unit, so each is a single observation; gold writes them as members of the same set as the measured values, in the spirometry file. Kept as a set because V2 does so; Anne to confirm (see questions).

Example source variable description: Predicted FEV1, liters|Predicted FVC, liters|Predicted FEV1/FVC
